s: A dedicated entry point for AI/ML workloads that provides unified routing, authentication, rate limiting, cost tracking, and policy enforcement for all LLM and model API calls.
w: Sits between application services and model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, self-hosted). The gateway normalizes heterogeneous provider APIs into a single interface, enforces authentication and authorization, applies per-user or per-team rate limits and token budgets, logs all requests for audit and cost analysis, routes to different providers based on model, region, or fallback rules, and optionally transforms requests/responses for provider-specific quirks. Unlike a general API gateway, it is purpose-built for streaming, token-based metering, and model-specific concerns.
use: Centralizing LLM access control, key management, and audit logging
Cost governance with per-team token budgets and usage dashboards
Provider failover and load balancing across multiple LLM backends
Abstraction layer so application code is provider-agnostic
avoid: Simple single-provider setups where direct API calls are simpler
Scenarios where the gateway itself becomes a single point of failure without HA
Ultra-low-latency requirements where an extra network hop is unacceptable

props.rate_limit_rpm: Requests per minute cap per key or user
props.token_budget: Maximum tokens consumable per time window
props.fallback_chain: Ordered list of providers for automatic failover

pat.d: Route same prompt to multiple providers in parallel, return first response (speculative execution).
Cache LLM responses keyed by normalized prompt + model to avoid redundant inference calls.

pits: Gateway as single point of failure - deploy with redundancy and circuit breakers to providers
Streaming response buffering defeats the purpose - gateway must pass SSE/chunks through without buffering
Stale provider key rotation causing 401s - implement proactive key refresh
tips: Track cost per request and per user at the gateway - this is the primary governance value
Use the gateway for semantic caching which can reduce LLM spend by 30-60% on repeated queries
Gateway enables A/B testing of models by routing percentage of traffic to different providers
